function: Learned joint NOMA power allocation and IRS mirror orientation (roll, yaw) maximizing sum energy efficiency times Jain fairness, p. 5.
system: Indoor VLC downlink: 4 LED APs, 5 users (Table I: 8) with angle diversity receivers, passive 7x7 mirror-array IRS (reflecting), visible light, 20 MHz, pp. 3, 8-9.
method: Two-agent actor-critic deep reinforcement learning (deterministic policy gradient, fully connected networks), centralized training with decentralized execution, 2000 training episodes in simulation, pp. 6-9.
data_channel: Custom indoor VLC simulator: Lambertian LoS channel [34] plus specular mirror NLoS channel [5], 5x5x3 m room, random-waypoint users, pp. 3, 8.
test_conditions: Single simulated room with random-waypoint users (0-2 m/s); no separate test scenario; sweeps over optical power, mirror count, users, Rmin, pp. 8-11.
baselines: Standard DDPG and DQN (learned); fixed power allocation; DDPG power with fixed or random IRS orientation; DDPG without IRS, pp. 10-11.
metrics: Sum energy efficiency, sum rate, Jain fairness index, mean reward during training, pp. 5, 9-11.
complexity: Orders of actor and critic networks of both agents, e.g. actor O((2K+2M)×K) and O(3K×2M); no runtime or parameter count, p. 8.
openness: none; p. 11 states only that all data are in the results section, with no code or data link.
q1_support: p. 8: "We consider an indoor room with a size of (5m×5m×3m)"; custom VLC simulator (Lambertian LoS channel [34], mirror NLoS channel [5], p. 3). Missing: any 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "Fig. 7 shows the impact of the IRS mirror number on the sum rates of the schemes considered." Figs. 6 to 8 only sweep power, M, K and Rmin; the paper never reports testing a trained agent on unseen settings (p. 8: "state dimension equals to 2K + 2M" ties the networks to K and M).
q3_support: p. 10: "compared to other standard DRL algorithms such as DDPG and DQN algorithms" (SEE, sum rate); p. 11: "compared to the fixed power allocation scheme" (fairness) and "baseline 2, in which the IRS configuration is randomly selected" (sum rate).
q4_support: p. 8: "the complexity of the actor-network is O((2K + 2M ) × K)"; orders given for the actor and critic of both agents (Section IV-E).
q5_support: p. 11: "All data are provided in full in the results section of this paper." Missing: a code or data link or DOI; own simulator in Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.0 (p. 9) and no public channel dataset.
notes: Optical (VLC) system with a passive mirror-array IRS instead of an RF RIS: no exclusion code applies (area 3: IRS configuration by mirror roll and yaw angles, plus NOMA power allocation), so the reviewer should confirm scope. Text gives K = 5 users (p. 8) but Table I lists 8 (p. 9). Baselines 2 and 3 of Fig. 6 use DDPG for power, so the non-learned comparison rests on the fixed power allocation of Fig. 9 (p. 11) and the fixed or random IRS orientation of baseline 2 (pp. 10-11). Fig. 7 legend prints Baseline 3 twice (p. 10). The PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (2504.18937, 26 Apr 2025) and prints no DOI.
